task_instance: Set up and run a mewt mutation testing campaign on a small Rust crate (sample_crate) with a deliberate testing gap (an untested boundary condition in is_adult() and partially-tested branches in max_of_three()), then read back and interpret the results.
tools_used: mewt CLI (init, mutate, run, status, results, print mutant)
evidence: Installed mewt 4.0.0 via the official installer script (curl ... mewt-installer.sh | sh) into /root/.cargo/bin. Created a minimal Rust lib crate at sample_crate/ with functions add, is_adult (boundary check >=18 deliberately under-tested), and max_of_three (branches partially untested), plus unit tests covering only some paths (cargo test: 3 passed). Ran `mewt init` to generate mewt.toml/mewt.sqlite, set targets.include = ["src/**/*.rs"] and test.cmd = "cargo test", then `mewt mutate` generated 33 mutants (5 high, 10 medium, 18 low severity) and `mewt run` executed the full campaign (baseline passed, 22 mutants tested, 13 caught, 9 uncaught, 1 timeout, 10 skipped in ~16s). Verified via `mewt status` (per-target and campaign-wide breakdown with catch rates) and `mewt results` (default uncaught view) which correctly surfaced exactly the deliberately-introduced testing gaps: mutant IDs 20/23 (COS mutation changing 'age >= 18' to '!=' / '>' on the is_adult boundary), mutant IDs 12/14/15 (IF/IT mutations on the untested max_of_three branches), and CR (comment-out) mutations on lines whose assertions weren't exercising all effects. Confirmed `mewt results --format json` produces well-formed structured output with mutant/target/outcome fields, and `mewt print mutant --id 20` correctly displays the mutated source showing 'age != 18'. Deliverable (a real, executed mutation testing campaign with interpretable survivor results matching the skill's documented workflow) exists at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/trailofbits__skills__mutation-testing/sample_crate/ (mewt.toml, mewt.sqlite, src/lib.rs).
